subject: PO vs Card — procurement next steps & vendor onboarding
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@fintechco.com>, Thomas Li <t.li@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: PO vs Card — procurement next steps & vendor onboarding

Hi Elena / Thomas,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the deep dive on your integration needs and the procurement constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the commercial path: 

Call recap:
- FintechCo is evaluating a Redwood Dedicated deployment for latency-sensitive production workloads.
- Primary blockers: vendor onboarding (legal, W9, SOC 2) and AP payment method (PO vs corporate card) for initial procurement.
- You’re also evaluating whether to buy via your cloud marketplace or via direct invoice.

Proposed next steps / asks from FintechCo:
1) Can you confirm AP's preferred payment method for this engagement (PO/invoice vs credit card) and any threshold where PO is required?
2) Does procurement prefer marketplace purchases (e.g., CloudMarket) for faster procurement or do you need direct invoicing to your vendor portal?
3) Please share the vendor onboarding packet or any specific forms we should complete.

What I’m attaching: vendor_onboarding_checklist.pdf (fillable checklist) and redwood-sla-summary.pdf. I’ve also linked our most recent SOC 2 Type II report above. We can provide a W9 and insurance certificate immediately.

If it helps, we can do a short follow-up with procurement on Friday to walk through the vendor steps live — Rishi (cc'd) can join on implementation/onboarding timelines.

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- This week: confirm payment method and share procurement packet.
- Next week: Redwood provides W9 + SOC 2 link + redwood order form.
- 1-2 weeks after PO execution: kickoff Dedicated provisioning and onboarding.

Let me know your preferred time for a procurement call.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

From: Elena Park <elena.park@fintechco.com>

Cc: FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>, Thomas Li <t.li@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO vs Card — procurement next steps & vendor onboarding

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the summary and the attachments — very helpful. A few notes from procurement / AP perspective: 

1) Payment method: Our AP policy is to use corporate card for ad-hoc SaaS purchases under $5,000. For anything expected to exceed $5k in a 12-month period we require a PO/invoice routed through our vendor portal. Given the scope you outlined, this will likely need a PO.

2) Marketplace: Procurement prefers marketplace purchases when available because it shortens the time to pay, but there is an additional marketplace fee and limitations around custom SLAs. If Redwood is listed on CloudMarket (or equivalent), we can evaluate that path — our procurement team will still need vendor onboarding documents.

3) Vendor onboarding requirements: We will need
   - Completed vendor packet (see attached FintechCo_vendor_packet.pdf)
   - W9 (US companies)
   - SOC 2 Type II report
   - Proof of general liability insurance

4) Timeline: If you can return the W9 + SOC2 link + completed packet by EOD Tuesday, we can get the vendor set up and (assuming no legal redlines) issue a PO within 5-7 business days.

Questions for you: Do you have a standard order form / SOW template we should expect? Also, if we go marketplace route, can you confirm whether Redwood's SLAs are still honored (i.e., no SLA degradation) and whether pricing is identical?

Cc'ing Thomas in procurement for visibility.

Thanks,

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Procurement | FintechCo
elena.park@fintechco.com
(212) 555-0199

Attachment: FintechCo_vendor_packet.pdf

Subject: Re: PO vs Card — procurement next steps & vendor onboarding

Elena — thanks, this is perfect and very actionable. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Payment & order flow: We fully support both PO/invoice and credit card. For PO workflow we contract on our standard order form (attached as a draft in the next email if helpful) and invoice per the payment terms you specify. For marketplace purchases we are listed on CloudMarket and can confirm that our standard SLAs still apply for marketplace orders — pricing can differ slightly due to marketplace fees; happy to share options.

2) Docs we will provide by EOD Tuesday: W9, insurance certificate, link to SOC 2 Type II report (https://redwood.inference/soc2-report), and a completed vendor onboarding checklist.

3) Order form / SOW: I’ll attach our standard order form and a short SOW template in a separate email for legal to review. If procurement prefers, we can accept a PO referencing our order form and proceed without a separate DocuSign step, or we can run the order via DocuSign — whichever fits your vendor portal.

4) Next call: Rishi and I are available Friday 9-11am PT to walk procurement through the packet and answer any implementation questions. Please let us know if that works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

We’ll upload the documents to the HubSpot deal record and share the DocuSign link once the order form is ready: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/FIN-7890

Appreciate the clarity — we’ll get the items over to you on Tuesday and follow up for the PO issuance timeline.

Best,
